title: The time the x86 emulator team found code so bad they fixed it during emulation
summary: A historical anecdote from Microsoft's x86 emulator team describing a case where they encountered code so poorly written that they chose to patch it on-the-fly during emulation rather than trying to fix the underlying source, showcasing pragmatic problem-solving in legacy system emulation.
problem_solved: Deals with executing extremely buggy legacy x86 code that couldn't be fixed at the source but needed to run correctly in an emulator.
why_valuable: Demonstrates real-world pragmatic engineering decisions when maintaining emulators, showing how teams balance correctness with practicality when dealing with decades-old legacy code.
